34.threads: Korea's July monsoon catches more travelers off guard than winter cold does. Pack a compact umbrella over a heavy raincoat for summer — humidity makes rain gear miserable fast. Winter (Dec-Feb) needs real layering, especially outside Seoul. Which season are you flying in?
34.facebook:
Packing for Korea depends more on the month than most guides admit. 🌦️

1. Summer (Jun-Aug): hot and humid with a real monsoon in July — go light and breathable, skip the heavy raincoat.
2. Winter (Dec-Feb): dry and cold, with heavier snow outside Seoul than most visitors expect.
3. Spring/fall: the easiest weather, but also the most crowded for walking-heavy days.

Check: humidity gear for summer, real layers for winter.
What month are you visiting?

36.source: KTX vs. SRT vs. intercity bus for long-distance travel
36.threads: Most first-timers don't know SRT exists — they just know KTX. Both are high-speed rail Seoul-to-Busan, but KTX leaves from Seoul Station and SRT from Suseo Station, so your starting point decides the better pick. Which station is closer to where you're staying?
36.facebook:
The real choice for Seoul-to-Busan isn't train vs. bus — it's KTX vs. SRT. 🚄

1. KTX departs mainly from Seoul Station; SRT from Suseo Station — pick based on which side of the city you're on.
2. Both are similar-speed high-speed rail on comparable routes.
3. Both require a booked seat and departure time, unlike a hop-on intercity bus.

Check which station is closer before you book.

There's a second high-speed train most first-timers never hear about.

37.facebook:
Mobile data in Korea has a cheap trap most groups fall into. 📶

1. No eSIM support? Physical SIM or Wi-Fi egg counters are at both Incheon and Gimpo arrivals.
2. Reserve online ahead of time for a discount and shorter line.
3. Pocket Wi-Fi lets a whole group share one connection instead of buying separate SIMs.
4. Return the egg at the airport counter or a marked drop box — miss it and a late fee kicks in.

40.facebook:
Korea is one of the safer destinations out there — but 'safe' still needs a few habits. 🛡️

1. Low violent crime rates, even late at night in major cities.
2. Still watch for pickpockets in crowded markets.
3. Keep an eye on your drink in nightlife areas.
4. Register with your home country's embassy alert service for real-time notices during your stay.

The 'best' airport transfer from Incheon depends entirely on your landing time. ✈️

1. Kakao T works at both ICN and GMP, often cheaper than flagging a taxi, with fares shown upfront.
2. Landing after trains stop for the night? A licensed airport taxi or pre-booked private transfer is the safe call.
3. Traveling as a group? A shared van booked in advance can beat several taxis on cost per person.

Skip the unmarked cars offering rides in the arrivals hall.

42.threads: Tipping in Korea doesn't just go unused — it can actively confuse the person you hand it to. Escalators have a standing side by local custom (varies by city). Many small restaurants are cash-preferred, with no split-bill custom. Which would've surprised you most?
42.facebook:
A few Korea etiquette habits catch almost every first-timer off guard. 🙇

1. Tipping isn't expected — it can actually confuse staff.
2. Escalators have a standing side by local custom, though it varies by city.
3. Many small restaurants are cash-preferred or card-only, with no split-bill custom.
4. Shoes usually come off indoors at traditional guesthouses and floor-seating restaurants.

Save this before your first trip.
